gap: No result ChatGPT got explains how SIMs work in these cameras. Spypoint installs and pre-activates the SIMs itself, so its free 100-photo plan runs on Spypoint's SIM and not one you buy. For the 'bring your own prepaid SIM' route that ChatGPT suggested, a US camera maker (Reolink) tells buyers to register the SIM with their phone's IMEI instead of the camera's, and says its 4G cameras do not support 5G.
standout_why: I compared against the two cited pages (the Spypoint FLEX-M product page and Spypoint blog id=259) and two top results (trailcamspecs.com and camandcanopy.com). The FLEX-M page only says the camera 'comes pre-loaded with two preactivated SIM cards' and offers 'cross-carrier coverage'. Blog 259 covers prices only. Trailcamspecs does not mention using your own SIM, carrier compatibility, IMEI or LTE-M. Cam & Canopy notes single versus dual SIM but nothing on SIM lock-in, IMEI registration or own-SIM compatibility. None of them warns that a prepaid SIM bought for a camera may need to be registered under a phone's IMEI, or that the camera must be on 4G, not 5G.
decides: This supports the Spypoint pick for 'free photos to my phone'. The free plan works because Spypoint supplies and activates the SIMs, so the shopper never deals with a carrier. It also weakens ChatGPT's second option ('use my own SIM card and prepaid data'). That route only works if the camera takes a standard Nano SIM on a 4G network and the carrier accepts it. Reolink's own instruction is to register the SIM with a phone's IMEI, which shows the camera's IMEI may not be accepted. The page should tell own-SIM shoppers to check that before buying, and should not present own-SIM as the zero-subscription default.

findings.label: Registering a user SIM with a US carrier
findings.value: "Use the IMEI code of your phone, not the camera's IMEI, when registering the SIM card." "Reolink 4G cameras are compatible only with 3G or 4G networks, and do not support 5G." The SIM must be a Nano SIM. Tested: T-Mobile prepaid data-only, Mint, FreedomPop (AT&T-based, APN 'ERESELLER' for Go PT). For Verizon: 'we recommend testing it with your camera'
findings.source_title: How to Choose SIM Card in the United States | Reolink Support
findings.note: Reolink is a camera maker, not a trail-camera brand, but this is the only maker statement I found on the own-SIM mechanism in the US. The IMEI instruction implies carriers check the IMEI at registration and the camera's own IMEI may not pass. The page shows no last-updated date (footer © 2026). The text also says T-Mobile's 3G UMTS network has been retired.
